statement: The line $L$ passes through $A(1,2)$ and is perpendicular to the line joining $B(3,1)$ and $C(5,7)$. Find the equation of $L$ and the coordinates of its intersection with $BC$.
solution:
The gradient of $BC$ is $\dfrac{7-1}{5-3}=3$, so the gradient of the perpendicular line $L$ is $-\tfrac13$.
Through $A(1,2)$:
$$y-2=-\tfrac13(x-1)\quad\Rightarrow\quad x+3y=7.$$
The line $BC$ has equation $y-1=3(x-3)$, i.e. $y=3x-8$. Substituting into $x+3y=7$:
$$x+3(3x-8)=7\quad\Rightarrow\quad 10x=31\quad\Rightarrow\quad x=\tfrac{31}{10},\quad y=3\left(\tfrac{31}{10}\right)-8=\tfrac{13}{10}.$$
The intersection point is $\left(\tfrac{31}{10},\tfrac{13}{10}\right)$.
hints: Use the negative reciprocal for the perpendicular gradient.
Solve the two line equations simultaneously.
